description: Stereo filter carrying the whole collection of Vult filter models, running the same code as the Vult hardware module, with the hardware's own menu system on its screen

params.text: Boosts the frequencies near the cutoff, and past a point the filter self-oscillates and can be played as a sound source
Sets the frequency at which the filter starts to act: fully counter-clockwise it is closed, fully clockwise it is open
Sets how much signal enters the filter, and raising it saturates the filter and adds harmonics
Attenuates and inverts the RES input before it is added to the resonance
Attenuates and inverts the A input before it is added to the cutoff
Attenuates and inverts the CUTOFF input before it is added to the cutoff, and a 1V/octave signal through it makes the cutoff track pitch
Attenuates and inverts the B input before it is added to the cutoff
Attenuates and inverts the DRIVE input before it is added to the drive
Steps through the filter models, among Vortex, Unstabile, Lateralus, Tangents, Stabile, Ferox, Nurage, Rescomb and Vorg
Steps through the responses of the filter model in use, such as lowpass, bandpass or highpass
Opens the hardware's own menu on the screen, which carries the settings that the right-click menu also lists

inputs.text: The left channel of the audio input
The right channel of the audio input
A control voltage added to the resonance, scaled by the RES attenuverter
A control voltage for the cutoff, scaled by the A attenuverter
A control voltage added to the cutoff, scaled by the CUTOFF attenuverter, and tracking 1V per octave when that attenuverter is set for it
A control voltage for the cutoff, scaled by the B attenuverter
A control voltage added to the drive, scaled by the DRIVE attenuverter

outputs.text: The left channel of the filtered signal
The right channel of the filtered signal

menu: MODE — arranges the two filter channels: STEREO puts one filter across a stereo pair, DUAL gives two independent filters, DUPLEX-S chains them in series and DUPLEX-P runs them in parallel
VCA — assigns an amplifier to the filter outputs: NO VCA, drive on both channels, or resonance on the left and drive on the right
MOD RANGE — sets the voltage the modulation inputs expect, 10V or 5V
OUT RANGE — attenuates the outputs to 100%, 70% or 30%
STEREO MOD — applies the modulation across the pair: NORMAL, INVERTED or SUMMED
MIX OUTPUT — blends the stereo pair towards mono: STEREO 0%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75% or MONO 100%
